- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3–4% above peak or use lagged mean.
- If model forecast is significantly above true outcome (e.g., >10% over 3–5 days), check sentiment for bullish bias — if bullish, reduce forecast by 5–10% to align with mean reversion.
- If model forecast is consistently below true outcome (e.g., -5%+ over 3–5 days), sentiment may be bearish — increase forecast by 5–10% if sentiment turns neutral or bullish.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-period momentum; add 1–2% lagged 15-day average to forecast if sentiment is bullish.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model tends to be noisy — use median of 3–5 recent forecasts or apply smoothing filter to reduce volatility.
